postings.title: Senior Mesh Network and MAC Engineer (All Genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a defence technology company redefining the engineering and deployment of autonomous platforms. Our core mission is to deliver fully operational unmanned systems, integrating the critical subsystems, including Electronic Warfare, necessary for NATO forces to maintain a decisive advantage in contested environments. We do whatever is required to achieve platform autonomy, grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.

About the team

We are a lean, agile group with a strong systems-minded focus. We operate without silos, looking for proactive engineers who are excited to take mathematical models off the whiteboard and deploy them onto physical hardware. On our Electronic Warfare algorithms team, you will bridge the gap between theoretical signal processing and real-world hardware execution, taking direct ownership of key software and firmware modules.

Your mission

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world's most contested environments. As a Senior Mesh Network and MAC Engineer you will solve the critical challenges of directional wireless communication in highly dynamic networks. You will design and implement the medium access control (MAC) and routing layers that allow our platforms to form robust, self-healing networks under demanding tactical conditions.

Responsibilities

- Architect and implement MAC protocols and routing algorithms tailored for directional multi-node systems, directly tackling the challenge of neighbour discovery under highly focused, narrow beams.
- Build dynamic TDMA schedules and beam coordination mechanisms in lockstep with the physical layer (PHY) and antenna steering systems, ensuring routing decisions are grounded in real-time RF characteristics rather than simple hop counts.
- Deliver resilient multi-hop relay capabilities that sustain high-bandwidth video and control links between mobile platforms over tactical distances, routing back seamlessly to ground control stations under dynamic conditions.
- Build and maintain multi-node Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testbeds alongside automated logging pipelines to quantitatively evaluate and verify network join times and topology reform behaviours.
- Mesh networking in a product that shipped — sim work alone does not qualify — plus Linux networking at kernel and packet level with live debugging.
- Radio-literate and has designed a medium-access scheme or TDMA schedule.

Qualifications

- You have successfully designed and shipped mesh networking protocols in commercial or defence products.
- Deep, practical familiarity with the Linux networking stack at the kernel and packet levels, coupled with strong live-debugging skills on embedded systems.
- Strong understanding of wireless propagation and physical layer realities, with hands-on experience designing medium-access control schemes or TDMA schedulers.

Nice to have

- Active contributions to open-source routing protocols (e.g., batman-adv, olsrd, Babel).
- A professional background at tactical mesh vendors (such as Silvus, Persistent Systems, TrellisWare, Saab, or Bittium).
- Experience with mmWave backhaul systems or other technologies where directional beamforming is the default mode of operation.
- Batman-adv / olsrd / Babel contributor; tactical mesh vendor background (Silvus, Persistent, TrellisWare, Saab, Bittium); mmWave backhaul — already thinks in beams.

- Maintain an awareness of civil aviation safety standards from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), particularly in areas like Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) or other relevant regulations, to address potential dual-use or operational safety aspects in controlled airspace.

- Translate customer (NATO/military) and statutory safety requirements into verifiable system and subsystem requirements.

- Participate in design reviews, test readiness reviews, and acceptance boards as the safety Subject Matter Expert (SME).

- Support the company's OHS program, ensuring compliance with German Occupational Safety Law (Arbeitssicherheitsgesetz - ASiG) and related regulations for handling ordnance and operating complex machinery.

- Define and implement internal safety processes, tools, and best practices to continually improve the company's safety culture and management system.

Qualifications

- Knowledge of German defense and ordnance safety regulations, as well as an awareness of EASA safety standards and their potential relevance to UAV/munition systems.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent communication and presentation abilities, and the capacity to work effectively in interdisciplinary, multi-national teams.

- Willingness to undergo necessary security clearance checks (ZÜP).

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer – Integration and Deployment (All Genders)
postings.description:
About Us

Über STARK
STARK ist ein neuartiges Defence-Tech-Unternehmen, das die Art und Weise revolutioniert, wie autonome Systeme in unterschiedlichen Einsatzdomänen eingesetzt werden. Wir entwickeln, konstruieren und produzieren hochleistungsfähige unbemannte Systeme, die softwaredefiniert, skalierbar in der Massenproduktion und kosteneffizient sind. Dadurch verschaffen wir unseren Anwendern einen entscheidenden Vorteil in hochumkämpften Einsatzumgebungen.

Unser Fokus liegt auf einsatzbereiten Hochleistungssystemen – nicht auf Zukunftsversprechen. In einer Zeit zunehmender Bedrohungen stärkt STARK den technologischen Vorsprung der NATO-Verbündeten und ihrer Partner, um Aggressionen abzuschrecken und Europa schon heute zu verteidigen.
Über das Team

Minerva ist die Command-and-Control-Software (C2) von STARK – das „Gehirn“, das Operatoren in Echtzeit mit autonomen Systemen über verschiedene Domänen hinweg verbindet. Das Minerva-Team ist eine kleine, hochqualifizierte Gruppe erfahrener Softwareentwickler mit Standorten in Berlin und München. Es arbeitet eng mit den Hardware- und Systemteams zusammen, um missionskritische C2-Fähigkeiten zu entwickeln, die in realen operativen Umgebungen eingesetzt werden.

Wir arbeiten schnell, liefern echte Software aus und bewegen uns in Rahmenbedingungen, die die meisten Softwareingenieure nie erleben: Netzwerke mit geringer Bandbreite, isolierte (air-gapped) Systeme und hochkritische Entscheidungsprozesse. Bei uns gibt es keine technische Spielerei ohne praktischen Nutzen. Alles, was wir entwickeln, landet direkt in den Händen von Anwendern im Einsatz.
Deine Mission

About the team

Wir suchen einen Senior Software Engineer (all genders), der das technische Gesicht von Minerva Frontline gegenüber unseren internen Hardware-Teams, Pilotkunden und Programmpartnern ist. Du bringst Frontline in neue interne und kundenseitige Projekte, verantwortest die technische Integration und gewinnst Vertrauen durch technische Exzellenz – nicht durch Projektmanagement. Wir sind als Team füreinander da!

Your mission

Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle zwischen Software, Hardware und operativer Realität: Du setzt das C++-Backend auf, das UAV-Schwärme orchestriert, integrierst neue Plattformen in laufende Systeme und stellst sicher, dass die Führungs- und Kontrollprozesse auch in isolierten, bandbreitenlimitierten taktischen Umgebungen reibungslos funktionieren.

Wenn im Feld etwas ausfällt, bist du vor Ort und behebst das Problem – unter Zeitdruck und mit dem Kunden direkt an deiner Seite.

Responsibilities

Integration und Deployment
- Installation, Konfiguration und Inbetriebnahme von Minerva Frontline in Kundenumgebungen.
- Arbeit mit Edge-Hardware, eingeschränkten Netzwerken und taktischer Infrastruktur.
- Integration neuer UAV-Plattformen und Funktionen in die Frontline-Plattform.

Analyse und Fehlerbehebung
- Technische Ansprechperson vor Ort für komplexe Systemprobleme.
- Analyse und Behebung von Problemen wie:
- Ausfällen oder Verschlechterungen der Schwarm-Telemetrie
- gRPC-Konnektivitätsproblemen
- Fehlern bei der Übersetzung von MAVLink-Kommandos in reale Drohnenaktionen

- Fehlerdiagnose und Problemlösung in Echtzeit.

Schnittstelle zwischen Kunde und Entwicklung
- Übersetzung von Feedback von Operatoren, Piloten und Kunden in konkrete technische Anforderungen.
- Enge Zusammenarbeit mit den Engineering-Teams zur Umsetzung von Verbesserungen, Fehlerbehebungen und Plattformintegrationen.

Validierung im Einsatz
- Teilnahme an Flugtests und Erprobungskampagnen.
- Sicherstellung, dass Softwarebefehle zuverlässig und präzise in physische Drohnenaktionen umgesetzt werden – auch unter realen Einsatzbedingungen.

Entwicklung von Tools
- Entwicklung eigener Werkzeuge, wenn Standardlösungen nicht ausreichen:
- Skripte
- Diagnose-Tools
- Integrations- und Testumgebungen

- Ziel ist es, Deployments reproduzierbar, effizient und robust zu gestalten.

Arbeit auf dem Feld
- Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit Hardware-Ingenieuren, Drohnenplattformen und Testequipment.
- Regelmäßige Einsätze bei Kunden und auf Testgeländen gehören fest zum Aufgabenbereich.

Qualifications

- Bachelor- oder Masterabschluss in Informatik, Robotik, Systems Engineering oder vergleichbare praktische Erfahrung.
- Sehr gute Kenntnisse in modernem C++ (C++17/20/23).
- Sicher im Lesen, Debuggen und Anpassen produktiver C++-Codebasen.
- Erfahrung im Aufbau und Betrieb komplexer verteilter Systeme.
- Praktische Kenntnisse in:
- Echtzeitfähigen verteilten Systemen
- gRPC
- Flatbuffers
- WebSockets
- MAVLink / MAVSDK

- Nachweisbare Erfahrung bei der Einführung und dem Betrieb von Softwarelösungen bei externen Kunden.
- Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Hardware-Teams während Flugtests und Plattformintegrationen.
- Bereitschaft zu regelmäßigen Reisen innerhalb Deutschlands (bis zu 40 %).
- Aufgrund der Art unserer Arbeit müssen Kandidatinnen und Kandidaten die Voraussetzungen für eine entsprechende Sicherheitsüberprüfung erfüllen.

Interessiert?
Wenn du gemeinsam mit uns die Zukunft der europäischen Verteidigung gestalten möchtest und dich in dieser Beschreibung wiederfindest, freuen wir uns auf deinen Lebenslauf in englischer Sprache.
Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Deine Ansprechpartnerin ist Sally Grütte-Pad, Interim Lead TA via talent@stark-defence.com

You will be joining a highly agile and multidisciplinary group that works closely with subsystem owners, safety engineers, and product management to ensure total coverage of operational needs. We thrive on direct collaboration, rapid iteration, and maintaining robust traceability from Concept of Operations (ConOps) down to L3 technical requirements.

Your mission

As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will drive the development and maintenance of our system architecture and requirement baselines. You will coordinate with hardware and software teams to allocate subsystem requirements and technical requirements across critical elements like the airframe, Ground Control Station (GCS), and Flight Control systems. By establishing clear traceability and managing the Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP), you will enable STARK to deliver safe, highly reliable, and compliant defence technologies within aggressive timelines.

You will work across engineering disciplines to design, test and build top-of-the-line solutions to some of the largest challenges facing the defence sector. In addition to academic and industrial experience in any technical field, candidates should also possess excellent communication skills, and an aptitude for turning complex challenges into direct, actionable solutions.

Responsibilities

- Define, decompose, and document system-level requirements down to subsystem and technical requirements.
- Maintain and evolve system engineering artefacts for Loitering Munition Systems across various configurations.
- Work closely with software and hardware teams to define interfaces, ensuring accurate allocation of requirements to system architecture elements.
- Assist in generating safety documentation, such as the Systems Engineering Management Plan (SEMP), Traceability Matrices, and System Hazard Analyses in compliance with MIL-STD-882E and IEC61508.
- Assist in the definition of IV&V (Integration, Verification, and Validation) processes for ground and flight testing, ensuring all customer requirements are verifiably met.
- Maintain technical documentation, including test protocols, subsystem design documents, and the overall system design baseline.
- Help refine our Data Models and Systems Engineering workflows to balance rapid development with rigorous documentation and traceability.

Qualifications

- Degree (Bachelor) in Systems Engineering, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering or a related field (or comparable practical experience). Qualifications in other technical fields will be strongly considered if they demonstrate relevant skills.
- Experience managing complex requirements databases and traceability matrices (e.g., Jama Connect, DOORS).
- Strong understanding of Systems Engineering V-model processes, System Breakdown Structures (SBS), and requirements decomposition.
- Initial experience in system integration and working with communication protocols (e.g., CAN, DroneCAN, MAVLink, Ethernet) is an advantage.
- Strong articulation skills in English (at least CEFR B2) and ideally in German.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills are a must, as is a motivation and willingness to learn and grow in a dynamic, innovation-driven environment.
- Experience in at least one of the following technical skillsets: 3D CAD; CFD/FEA or similar simulation techniques; Systems modelling and analysis in MATLAB/Simulink/SysML or similar.
- Code development in object-oriented languages (e.g. C, Python, Java, Javascript); Flight or similar vehicle testing.

Nice to have

- German language proficiency (CEFR B1 or above).
- Industry certifications or qualifications in Systems Engineering (e.g. from INCOSE).
- Familiarity with defence or aerospace functional safety standards, particularly MIL-STD-882E or IEC61508.
- Familiarity with unmanned aerial systems (UAS), loitering munitions, and autopilot platforms (e.g., Ardupilot, PX4, DroneCore).

postings.description:

Your mission

We're not looking for someone who executes a spec. We're looking for someone who becomes the spec. Hand this person a napkin sketch, a rough idea, or a "we need something that can do X" — and they come back with a flying prototype, not a slide deck explaining why it's hard. This role exists for the person who's been building things in a garage, a workshop, or a shed for years because they couldn't not — and who's ready to point that obsession at Europe's defence capability instead of the next hobby build.

- Take a concept from clean sheet to flying hardware — concept, design, fabrication, integration, first flight — with minimal hand-holding.

- Set the technical approach when working across disciplines, and resolve design conflicts directly instead of escalating them.

- Turn "I just know how to do this" knowledge into documentation other engineers can actually build from.

- Unblock and mentor junior and mid-level engineers in design reviews and builds — no management title required.

- Flag technical, schedule, or process risk before anyone asks — silence isn't a strategy here.

- Iterate fast on field and test data without waiting for a retro to tell you what broke.

Qualifications

- A track record of owning a full build cycle — concept to flight-tested prototype — independently, on at least one UAV/UGV or comparable platform.

- Deep, hands-on experience with composites, mechanical assemblies, robotics, and embedded hardware — earned in a workshop, not from a manual.

- Sound judgment under ambiguity and time pressure: you know what's good-enough-to-test versus good-enough-to-deploy without being told.

- Experience working across engineering disciplines and resolving competing technical requirements yourself.

- A demonstrated instinct for mentoring or technically leading others, even informally.

postings.title: Senior Waveform Architect (All Genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a defence technology company redefining the engineering and deployment of autonomous platforms. Our core mission is to deliver fully operational unmanned systems, integrating the critical subsystems, including Electronic Warfare, necessary for NATO forces to maintain a decisive advantage in contested environments. We do whatever is required to achieve platform autonomy, grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.

About the team

We are a lean, agile group with a strong systems-minded focus. We operate without silos, seeking visionary technical leaders who can define long-term technology roadmaps while remaining deeply hands-on with complex engineering problems. On the Electronic Warfare team, you will hold the highest level of technical authority for our attack and countermeasure capabilities, driving multi-domain architectures directly onto the modern battlefield.

Your mission

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world's most contested environments. As a Senior Waveform Architect, you will own the entire development, architecture, and implementation of the waveform for our tactical anti-jam radio. In this critical role, you will ensure our communication links remain highly robust and operational under severe electronic countermeasure conditions.

Responsibilities

- Lead the design and implementation of the physical layer (PHY)—waveform, modulation, coding, framing, and synchronisation—from initial architecture to real-time execution.
- Engineer solutions specifically tailored for challenging jamming scenarios and complex, multi-node long-range link budgets.
- Own the PHY-side specifications and expose the critical IQ, phase, and timing observables required by the Direction Finding (DF) strand.
- Define the development guidelines for the strand—including HDL and verification conventions, as well as FPGA build flows.

Qualifications

- You have successfully designed a PHY and brought it onto FPGA/SoC hardware in real time.
- You are quantitatively sure-footed on synchronisation, estimation, FEC (Forward Error Correction), and link budgets.
- You have practical experience debugging real radio links against physical hardware.

Nice to have

- Experience with anti-jamming and LPI/LPD (Low Probability of Intercept/Detection) in a tactical context.
- A professional background at industry leaders.
- Publicly verifiable PHY implementation evidence (e.g., custom GNU Radio OOT modules or contributions to the RFSoC toolchain).

postings.description:

At STARK, we are building the next generation of autonomous platforms capable of navigating the world’s most contested environments. We are currently hiring for multiple Software Engineering positions where the primary mission is to ensure our fleet maintains command, control, and situational awareness against near-peer threats.

Electronic Warfare (EW) is at the heart of everything we do. We’re looking for engineers who are passionate about the electromagnetic spectrum and eager to join a team that lives and breathes RF. Whether you specialise in signal processing, communications, or EW effects, your background in EW and high-performance C++ is what matters most. We prioritise deep expertise and a drive to solve complex problems over meeting every single sub-specialty requirement.

- Design high-performance C++ software for real-time signal processing, waveform manipulation, and mission-critical EW functions.

- Develop anti-jamming techniques, frequency hopping (FHSS), and adaptive filtering to bypass active electronic countermeasures.

- Design algorithms for RF sensing, signal detection, and situational awareness to identify and neutralise threats in dynamic environments.

- Collaborate with hardware and systems teams to tune RF front-ends, ensuring software is perfectly calibrated to physical constraints.

- Own the stack from initial design and mathematical modelling to rigorous bench testing and field trials.

- Deep understanding of the electromagnetic spectrum, DSP, Fourier methods, and modulation theory (QAM, QPSK, OFDM).

- Experience with low-probability-of-intercept (LPI) links, digital modulation schemes, and the underlying physics of RF propagation.

- Proficiency in embedded systems, Linux networking, specifically regarding radio-based mesh networks or point-to-point links.

- Exposure to jamming theory, threat-driven RF effects, or cognitive radio for automated interference avoidance.

Qualifications

- Strong engineering skills at both the systems design and detailed implementation levels.

- Strong proficiency in modern C/C++ (memory management, concurrency, performance analysis).

- Significant interest in physics/RF or a strong preexisting understanding of RF processing fundamentals and the electromagnetic spectrum.

- Clear and structured communication skills for cross-functional technical collaboration.

Relevant Backgrounds

- High end system software engineering in any context where both details and system level architecture is critical to mission success

- SDR Development: Extensive experience with platforms like USRP, pluto SDR, LimeSDR and frameworks like GNU Radio.

- Advanced Engineering: Backgrounds in radio-waveform development, X-ray systems, or mathematically driven system design.

- High performance computing and software benchmarking experience.

- Familiarity with cryptographic standards for securing over-the-air transmissions.

- Custom protocol design for low-bandwidth, high-latency environments.

- Hands-on experience with RF waveform design or amateur radio.

- Strong interest in physics, electromagnetic propagation, and waveform engineering.

- Hands-on experience with RF waveform design and amateur radio.

- Familiarity with wireless & cable-borne data formats (QAM-64, QPSK).

- Exposure to jamming theory, threat-driven RF effects, and EW tactics.

- Experience in signal processing and mathematical modelling (Fourier methods, modulation theory, filtering, etc.).

postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionising the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective — providing operators with a decisive edge in contested environments.

About the team

Our team leads the independent validation and verification of complex software systems, bridging the gap between rigorous architectural requirements and deployed capabilities. We operate at the critical intersection of software development and system safety, ensuring every release meets the highest performance and reliability standards. You will work closely with cross-functional partners in sofware & hardware, and flight operations to maintain technical integrity in a fast-paced environment.

Your mission

As the Software IVV Lead, you will act as the independent software testing and verification authority, ensuring that the standards defined by our architecture are measurably adhered to, rigorously tested, and successfully audited. You will own the strategy, infrastructure, and execution of software validation and verification, serving as the ultimate quality gatekeeper for our software release candidates before they reach hardware integration and testing in the field.

Responsibilities

- Define the Test Strategy: Establish and enforce the overarching software testing frameworks and QA processes (based on ISTQB) across all software capability teams.

- Manage Test Infrastructure & Tooling: Oversee the setup and maintenance of software test environments and test data, ensure the qualification of testing tools, and lead the generation of audit-proof, revision-safe test evidence.

- Oversee V&V Execution: Supervise the validation and verification phases of the V-Model, ensuring rigorous unit, integration, and sub-system-level testing are completed before handing over to the Hardware integration and Flight Testing teams.

- Ensure Requirements Traceability: Deliver transparency in bidirectional traceability between Software Requirements, architectural design, implementation, and testing. Define and monitor the traceability processes in close collaboration with Software Configuration Management (SCM), ensuring operational compliance.

- Govern Defect & Deviation Management: Establish and oversee the interfaces and processes for defect, deviation, and problem management, ensuring all findings from testing are systematically tracked, evaluated, and resolved.

- Enforce Code Quality: Drive the adoption of strict coding standards (like MISRA for C++) using automated static analysis and code coverage metrics.

- Interface with Configuration Management: Verify compliance with defined SCM processes, auditing baselines, versions, reproducible builds, Software Configuration Indexes, and Release Packages to ensure they meet quality standards.

- Act as the Quality Gatekeeper: Provide independent quality gate approvals and formal release recommendations for software release candidates via the Engineering Change Request (ECR) process, while recognizing that the ultimate release decision resides with Product/Program Management.

- Manage Audits: Lead the preparation, execution, and follow-up for all internal software QA assessments and external regulatory audits.

Qualifications

- Proven experience in defining and enforcing software testing frameworks and QA processes based on ISTQB standards.

- Deep expertise in managing the validation and verification (V&V) phases of the V-Model for complex software systems.

- Hands-on experience with automated static analysis tools and enforcing coding standards such as MISRA for C++.

- Strong background in requirements traceability and managing the interface between Software Requirements and test execution.

- Solid knowledge of Software Configuration Management (SCM) processes, including version control, reproducible builds, and release auditing.

- Demonstrated capability in defect and deviation management, ensuring systematic tracking and resolution of software findings.

Nice to have

- Professional experience within the defense or aerospace sectors, working with safety-critical software systems.

- Familiarity with preparing for and leading external regulatory audits and internal quality assessments.

- Experience with flight testing operations or hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) integration environments.

This will be reporting into the Maritime Director.

Your mission

You will lead system-level integration for next-generation Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USV), ensuring all mechanical, electrical, and software subsystems operate as a single, mission-ready platform. As a Systems Engineer you will define architecture and interfaces, manage integration and verification activities, and drive system validation through sea trials and acceptance testing.

Responsibilities

- Serve as the system integration lead for USV product development and upgrades, owning overall platform coherency from concept through delivery.

- Work day-to-day within multidisciplinary teams (mechanical, electrical, control hardware, software, test) across the full lifecycle of USV design, integration, test and fielding.

- Conceptualise and capture system architecture for new platforms and for enhancements to existing platforms, producing technical trade studies, sizing and system performance assessments.

- Systems-level design of communications pathways, distribution and redundancy tactics
- Produce layout and system design plans, define Interface Control Documents (ICDs) and enforce interface control processes for mechanical, electrical and software subsystems.

- Lead Verification & Validation (V&V) and acceptance activities: author test plans and procedures for critical subsystems, schedule and run tests, and compile written test reports.

- Support bench builds and hardware integration, and conduct hands-on vessel testing (VLOS/BVLOS) including travel to test ranges and customer sites as required.

- Act as the technical interface between internal teams, suppliers and customers to coordinate payload integration, unique/custom hardware or software interfaces, and ensure on-time capability delivery.

- Perform data analysis to maximise uptime: review test telemetry, identify trends and failure modes, and contribute to predictive maintenance / reliability improvements.

Qualifications

- Degree (or equivalent) in Systems, Maritime, Aerospace, Electrical or a closely related Engineering discipline.

- Significant industry experience with demonstrable systems engineering responsibility on complex Autonomous systems platforms

- Strong practical experience integrating complex systems: power systems, RF/EMC, EO sensors, networking, embedded controllers and payload interfaces.
- Proven track record in applying V-Model techniques within an engineering design project

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; highly organised and detail-oriented.

- Ability to operate effectively in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and to travel within the UK/Europe for testing and integration.

- A genuine passion for system development, integration and testing and a collaborative, inclusive team approach.

- Ideally you will hold a UK Security clearance or be eligible to obtain UK defence clearance and be able to travel to the South West England area when required

Nice to have

- Maritime product development experience and familiarity with appropriate standards: MCT/IMO/DNV.

- Background in start-up or scale-up environments where rapid prototyping, iterative testing and pragmatic engineering decisions are typical.

Our Commitment to the Armed Forces Community

We are proud to hold the Bronze Award from the Defence Employer Recognition Scheme (ERS), reflecting our meaningful commitment and ongoing support for UK defence personnel. At our core, we believe in championing those who serve, those who have served, and their families. As part of this scheme, we are dedicated to providing an inclusive, supportive environment where members of the Armed Forces community can thrive and bring their invaluable skills to our team.

postings.title: Systems Integration & QA Engineer (All genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionising the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective — providing operators with a decisive edge in contested environments.

We are focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe, today.

About the team

Mission Simulation is STARK’s digital proving ground — the tactical environment where our entire ecosystem of UAVs, surface vessels, and EW systems converges. The Mission Simulation team is a small, specialized group based in Munich, working closely with our platform and C2 teams to integrate all multi-domain assets into high-fidelity, Software-in-the-Loop simulators.

We move fast, ship realistic environments, and build for three core purposes: rigorous testing, high-stakes demos, and tactical training. There is no room for gamification. We simulate the reality of combat — from complex swarm logic to EW degradation — ensuring that developers can fail fast, and real soldiers can train safely before hitting the battlefield.

Your mission

As a Systems Integration & QA Engineer, you are the critical link between our physical simulation hardware and our software development team. You will physically assemble our simulator setups and rigorously test the software environments running on them. By building our QA processes from the ground up, you ensure that every simulation runs flawlessly, and you provide highly detailed, actionable feedback to our software engineers before any system is used for high-stakes training or customer demos.

Responsibilities

- Assemble and configure physical simulator hardware setups, integrating PCs, networking gear, and tactical peripherals (e.g., VR, HOTAS) to create realistic testing environments.

- Execute comprehensive software testing within the Mission Simulation environment (e.g., VBS4, custom C++ modules) to identify bugs, performance bottlenecks, and tactical inaccuracies.

- Design and establish foundational QA testing protocols, test plans, and bug-tracking workflows from scratch.

- Collaborate directly with the software engineering team, translating simulator performance issues into clear, actionable technical feedback and bug reports.

- Validate software updates and new releases on the physical simulator setups to guarantee stability before they are deployed for customer demos or tactical training.

- Reproduce complex software and integration bugs systematically to assist developers in rapid resolution.

Qualifications

- Degree in IT, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- 3+ years of experience in software QA testing, system integration, or a similar role bridging IT hardware and software development.

- Hands-on experience assembling IT/simulator hardware and configuring operating systems (Windows and Linux).

- Proven ability to define and build QA processes, write structured test plans, and manage bug-tracking workflows.

- Strong technical communication skills to effectively translate user-end bugs into actionable data for software developers.

- Professional working proficiency in English (both spoken and written).

Nice to have

- Familiarity with simulation engines (e.g., VBS4, Unreal, Unity) or complex tactical gaming environments.

- Basic scripting skills (e.g., Python, PowerShell) to automate repetitive software testing or OS configuration tasks.

- Experience in the defense sector or foundational knowledge of military operations/tactics to help evaluate simulation realism.

postings.title: Test Design Engineer (All Genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a defence technology company redefining how autonomous and electronic warfare systems are engineered and deployed. We design, build, and operationalise high-performance EW and unmanned systems that provide NATO forces with decisive advantages in contested electromagnetic environments. Our work is grounded in precision, responsibility, and uncompromising engineering discipline.

Your mission

As a Test Design Engineer (Field Engineer) within the Electronic Warfare (EW) division, you will bridge the gap between development and real-world execution. This role is heavily focused on the test design, validation, and field deployment of advanced RF communications and electronic attack (jamming) systems. You will design rigorous test methodologies, simulate contested electromagnetic environments, and lead field-testing campaigns to ensure our technologies dominate the modern battlespace.

Responsibilities

- Develop comprehensive test plans, procedures, and automated test scripts for EW systems, specifically focusing on RF communications, signals intelligence (SIGINT), and electronic countermeasures (ECM/Jamming).

- Lead and execute field-testing campaigns in complex, dynamic, and austere environments. Troubleshoot hardware, software, and RF link issues on-site.

- Design and replicate real-world threat environments using RF signal generators, channel simulators, and software-defined radios (SDRs) to test jamming efficacy and communications resilience (e.g., frequency hopping, LPI/LPD waveforms).

- Collect, process, and analyze massive datasets from field tests using MATLAB, Python, or specialized RF analysis tools to quantify system performance and identify anomalies.

- Partner with systems, hardware, and software engineering teams to feed field data back into the development loop, driving iterative design improvements.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Telecommunications, Aerospace Engineering, or a highly related technical discipline.

- 3+ years of experience in RF engineering, flight test engineering, or electronic warfare testing.

- Strong foundational knowledge of RF propagation, link budgets, antenna characteristics, and modulation techniques (e.g., QAM, OFDM, FSK).

- Deep familiarity with laboratory and field test equipment, including Spectrum Analyzers, Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs), Signal Generators, and Oscilloscopes.

- Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW for test automation and post-test data analysis.

Nice to have

- Prior experience with specific electronic attack methodologies (e.g., barrage, spot, sweep, and DRFM-based jamming).

- Hands-on experience with Software Defined Radios (Ettus USRP, BladeRF) and tactile military communications networks.

- Familiarity with government test ranges (e.g., White Sands, China Lake) and range safety/operations protocols.

postings.title: UAV Operations Engineer / Pilot – Data Operations (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.

We're focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe — today.

About the team

The Data Operations team owns the entire data lifecycle behind STARK's AI stack: collection, acquisition, generation, curation, and management. We run our own data-collection campaigns across Europe, evaluate new sensors and platforms, and build the internal data platform that turns raw recordings into ready-to-use datasets. Everything we produce feeds directly into the perception and autonomy systems deployed on STARK's platforms — a real data advantage is built, not bought. The team is scaling up right now: real scope, direct impact, no legacy.

Your mission

You own our data-collection flights. When the perception team needs a specific dataset — a new camera at a new angle, a lidar over specific terrain, a thermal sensor at dusk — you plan the campaign, configure and tune the platform, fly the mission, and bring clean data home. Our hardware engineer builds the rigs and mounts, our robotics engineer makes the sensors record — you make it all fly, reliably, again and again. This is a role for someone with real stick time and real PX4/ArduPilot depth: not a desk job with occasional field trips, but the other way around.

Responsibilities

- Plan and execute field data-collection campaigns across Europe: flight planning, site assessment, pre-flight checks, piloting, logging, and post-flight data offload

- Configure, tune, and troubleshoot PX4/ArduPilot flight stacks for stable, repeatable data-collection flights

- Analyze flight logs to diagnose issues and continuously improve platform reliability

- Operate sensor payloads (cameras, gimbals, lidar, GNSS/IMU) during missions and verify recordings on-site

- Keep the fleet mission-ready: maintenance, repairs, spare parts, battery management, and configuration control

- Work with our hardware and robotics engineers on payload integration — you define what the platform needs to fly well

- Maintain flight logs and campaign documentation so every flight produces usable, traceable data

- Ensure operations comply with aviation regulations (EU drone rules) and internal safety procedures

Qualifications

- Confident, experienced drone pilot with substantial real-world flight hours (multirotor; fixed-wing a plus), holding an EU A2/A3 certificate or willing to obtain quickly

- Solid practical knowledge of PX4 and/or ArduPilot: configuration, parameter tuning, log analysis, MAVLink basics

- Hands-on experience assembling, repairing, and maintaining drones — comfortable with soldering, wiring, and multimeter debugging

- Experience operating sensor payloads and ground control stations in the field

- Practical, structured, and safety-conscious — you find the loose cable before it becomes a crash

- Willingness to travel regularly for field campaigns and work outdoors in various conditions

- Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Nice to have

- Scripting skills (Python, Bash) for flight log processing and data offload automation

- CAD basics (Fusion 360, SolidWorks) and 3D-printing experience

- Experience with ROS/ROS2 recording setups or companion computers (Jetson, Raspberry Pi)

- Background in FPV, drone racing, RC modeling, competition teams, or maker culture

- Experience with camera settings and image quality trade-offs for data collection

- German driving license class B (field campaigns)

A note on our process: a portfolio says more than a CV here. Show us your builds and your flights — photos, flight logs, competition entries. If you don't hit every bullet point but you have been flying and fixing drones for years, we still want to hear from you.
If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, please send us your CV and portfolio in English. We're looking forward to meeting you!

postings.title: UAV Pilot / GCS Operator (Production & Validation) Nordics
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company, revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.

We’re focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe.

Your mission

As a UAV Pilot / GCS Operator, your mission is to be the final gatekeeper of quality and safety. Working alongside Flight Test Engineers, you will lead the execution and reporting of production flight tests. Your role is to ensure that every system leaving our facility meets our rigorous performance standards and design specifications.

You will spend your days at the intersection of production and operations, monitoring live telemetry, validating autonomous behaviors, and providing the engineering team with the data they need to iterate. You aren't just operating a drone; you are certifying a capability that will be deployed in the world's most demanding environments.

Responsibilities

Production Flight Execution

- Conduct remote piloting and GCS operation for production-level unmanned aircraft.

- Execute standardized flight test programmes with high repeatability and precision to validate system performance.

- Monitor live telemetry and onboard video streams in real-time, ensuring flight conditions remain within the test envelope.

- Coordinate with observers and test engineers to maintain safe, efficient operations in a collaborative team environment.

System Preparation & Maintenance

- Perform pre-flight configurations, control link verifications, and comprehensive functional system checks.

- Assist in the ground verification of flight-critical hardware and software before takeoff.

- Maintain rigorous logbook standards and regulatory recordkeeping for every airframe tested.

Safety & Continuous Improvement

- Act as the tactical lead for airspace monitoring and deconfliction in accordance with SORA and EASA requirements.

- Respond decisively to flight anomalies and emergency situations by following established safety protocols.

- Contribute to the evolution of pilot training materials, safety documentation, and operational procedures.

Qualifications

Experience & Certifications

- Valid EU A1/A3 and A2 Remote Pilot Certificates (EASA).

- Valid radio operator certificate (e.g., BZF) or willingness to obtain one.

- Proven experience with professional GCS software, mission planning tools, and telemetry monitoring.

- Familiarity with flight safety protocols, particularly under BVLOS conditions.

- Must be a citizen of a NATO member state (due to export control and security regulations).

Technical Background

- High degree of comfort with structured, high-discipline test procedures.

- Ability to maintain deep situational awareness during long test sessions.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Familiarity with regulatory recordkeeping and post-flight documentation.

Mindset & Style

- Precision-Oriented: You find satisfaction in repeatability and "doing it right every time."

- Reliable: You are the person the team trusts to handle a $100k+ asset with care and discipline.

- Agile: You can pivot quickly when weather or production schedules shift.

Bonus Skills

- Previous experience as an RPIC for experimental drone testing.

- Practical knowledge of Ardupilot or PX4 autopilot systems.

- Background in military UAV operations or the defense sector.

postings.title: UAV Technician Nordics
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a defense technology company revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high performance unmanned vehicles that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost effective – giving NATO and its allies a decisive edge in the most contested environments.We’re focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems - not future promises. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe - today.

Your mission

As a UAV Technician, you will be the technical backbone of our flight test operations in the Nordics, specifically driving the development of the Virtus product line. Your mission is to ensure our platforms can withstand extreme cold and operate flawlessly. In addition, working in the Nordics will include utilizing systems adapted for Arctic climate.

Preferably you have built FPV copters, deeply understand UAV architectures, and can troubleshoot complex avionics on the fly.

You will face unpredictable challenges in harsh environments and solve them with a highly skilled team. You will be responsible for diagnosing issues, fine-tuning heating element settings, replacing components on the spot, and providing critical, documented feedback to the engineering team in Germany.

This is a highly versatile role. While your primary focus is technical troubleshooting and UAV maintenance, you will have the opportunity to expand your scope into other areas. Your work directly ensures that our systems are rugged, reliable, and ready for our Nordic customers.

Responsibilities

UAV Assembly, Integration & Troubleshooting

- Serve as the on-site technical expert for the Virtus platforms during flight testing.

- Diagnose, fix, and replace components on the fly (e.g., flight controllers, ESCs, brushless motors, heating elements).

- Fine-tune and troubleshoot anti-icing systems and cold-weather modifications directly in the field.

- Understand and debug low-level hardware communications, including CAN bus, PWM signals, and power distribution systems.

Flight Line & Technical Support

- Preparation of mission: prepare all tools and equipments required for the mission (pre-flight, troubleshooting and mechanical and electrical rework if it is needed)

- Pre-Flight Preparation: Support engineers and pilots during pre-flight checks: connecting and routing cables, managing battery charging systems, preparing airframes for test, and verifying ground support equipment readiness.

- Telemetry & Data Support: Learn to operate basic data logging and monitoring tools to support post-flight data checks and anomaly tracking.

- Airspace & Safety Assistance: Support safety procedures on-site including range clearance, observer duties, and adherence to SORA/EASA site safety requirements.

Flight Test Operations & Engineering Interface

- Act as the critical bridge between the Nordic flight test site and the engineering team in Germany.

- Meticulously document hardware failures, system behaviors in extreme cold, and on-site modifications.

- Take on Flight Test Engineer responsibilities: organize test requests, maintain test logs, and perform post-flight data analysis.

- Utilize Mission Planner and/or QGroundControl to extract, read, and interpret flight logs.

Your First 12 Months

Timeframe Focus

Month 0–1: Learn & Align

Understand the Virtus system architecture, engineering workflows, and cold-weather modifications. Get hands-on with our avionics stack, anti-icing systems, and telemetry setups. Familiarize yourself with our specific ArduPilot/PX4 configurations.

Month 1–3: Deploy & Troubleshoot

Deploy to the Nordics and spend much time at test sites. Support the initial arctic test campaigns. Focus heavily on troubleshooting heating elements, replacing components in the field, and establishing a robust feedback loop with the Engineering team and suppliers.

Month 3–6: Analyze & Optimize

Take ownership of flight test data organization. Analyze flight logs using Mission Planner/QGroundControl to identify performance degradation in cold weather. Begin cross-training as a GCS Operator or Safety Pilot, depending on your background.

Month 6–12: Scale & Mature

Establish a repeatable, reliable field-testing workflow for the arctic product line. Serve as the definitive technical authority on site. Fully integrate into Flight Test Engineering or Piloting roles to run autonomous missions from end to end.

Qualifications

Experience & Technical Background

- Deep, hands-on experience building, tuning, and repairing UAVs (e.g., FPV quadcopters, custom fixed-wing drones).

- Strong familiarity with open-source flight stacks, specifically ArduPilot and/or PX4.

- Intimate knowledge of UAV hardware architecture: Flight Controllers, ESCs, Brushless Motors, Lithium Batteries, CAN bus, and PWM.

- Experience with flight control software and ground stations, preferably Mission Planner and/or QGroundControl.

- Soldering skills and the ability to modify or repair electronics in field conditions.

Mindset & Working Style

- The Tinkerer’s Mindset: You love figuring out how things work and aren't afraid to tear a system down to fix it.

- Resilience & Pragmatism: Comfortable working outdoors in cold, harsh Norwegian environments, solving problems on the fly.

- Structured, meticulous, and rigorous in documenting technical issues and communicating them to remote engineering teams.

- Mission-driven, with a bias for fast iteration and practical, field-expedient solutions.

Location: Stockholm and Norway (Flight Test Site) with close ties to the Munich (Germany) Area HQ.

Nice to have

- RC Piloting experience (familiarity and ability to fly multirotors and/or fixed-wing aircraft manually, with and without stabilization).

- Previous experience as a Flight Test Engineer (managing test cards, data analysis, test planning).

- Experience with extreme cold weather operations, anti-icing systems, or thermal management in electronics.

- Background in defense, robotics, or aerospace testing.

postings.title: UAV Test Pilot (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company, revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective. This provides our operators with a decisive edge in highly contested environments.

We’re focused on delivering deployable, high-performance systems. In a time of rising threats, STARK is bolstering the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe.

Your mission

As a UAV Test Pilot at STARK, you are the critical link between digital design and physical reality. Working in lockstep with Flight Test Engineers, you will be responsible for the planning, execution, and reporting of flight tests for experimental, developmental, and modified production systems.

Your mission is to push our airframes to their limits to validate performance, ensure compliance with international standards, and prove the safety of our designs. You aren't just "flying drones", you are validating the next generation of autonomous flight technologies that will protect Europe. Whether you are executing high-performance manual maneuvers or monitoring complex BVLOS autonomous missions, your feedback will directly shape the software and hardware of the future.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities

Flight Operations & Execution

- Conduct remote piloting of unmanned aircraft during development and validation campaigns, often in full-manual mode to test the raw flight envelope.

- Execute flight tests with surgical precision according to the flight test programme.

- Monitor live telemetry and onboard video streams, maintaining total situational awareness of aircraft health and test status.

- Coordinate seamlessly with GCS operators, observers, and engineers in a high-pressure team environment.

Test Planning & Preparation

- Contribute operational expertise to test site selection, flight profiles, hazard analysis, and weather constraints.

- Prepare UAV systems, including pre-flight configuration, control link verification, and functional system checks.

- Assist with the integration and ground verification of flight-critical hardware and software.

Safety, Regulatory & Documentation

- Act as the final authority on safety for each sortie, conducting risk assessments and responding to anomalies or emergency situations.

- Maintain airspace deconfliction in accordance with SORA and EASA regulatory requirements.

- Participate in briefings/debriefings, providing structured, technical feedback on aircraft behavior.

- Support licensing and documentation to build long-term test capabilities across Germany and Europe.

Your First 12 Months

Timeframe

Focus

Month 0–1: Onboarding

Master the STARK tech stack. Get familiar with our current airframes, GCS software, and safety protocols. Complete local site inductions and shadow existing flight operations.

Month 1–3: Integration

Begin executing standard test cards. Support the engineering team in ground-testing new components and take your first "stick time" with experimental prototypes.

Month 3–6: Mission Lead

Lead flight test campaigns for specific subsystem validations. Contribute significantly to SORA applications and expand our operational footprint in Europe.

Month 6–12: Advanced Testing

Execute complex BVLOS and high-performance envelopes. Start transitioning toward Flight Test Engineering (FTE) tasks, including data analysis and test director responsibilities.

Qualifications

Experience & Certifications

- Valid EU A1/A3 and A2 Remote Pilot Certificates (EASA).

- Valid radio operator certificate (e.g., BZF) or the ability to obtain one immediately.

- Demonstrable manual piloting skills of high-performance fixed-wing and multirotor UAVs (precision take-offs, landings, and maneuvering in tight spots).

- Experience with professional GCS software, mission planning tools, and telemetry monitoring.

- Must be a citizen of a NATO member state (due to export control and security regulations).

Technical Mindset

- Familiarity with test operations under BVLOS and experimental conditions.

- Skilled in maintaining situational awareness during long, complex multi-aircraft operations.

- A problem-solving mindset—you don’t just report a bug; you help the engineers find the "why."

- Excellent written and verbal communication in English.

Mindset & Style

- Disciplined: You follow test cards to the letter but stay agile when a plan changes last minute.

- Reliable: High attention to detail with a "safety-first" internal compass.

- Startup Ready: You thrive in a fast-paced environment where your role evolves as the company grows.

Nice to Have

- Previous experience as a Flight Test Engineer or holding a PPL/CPL/ATPL.

- Hands-on experience tuning Ardupilot or PX4 autopilot systems.

- Background in military UAV operations or defense contracting.

Why STARK

- Shape the Future: A unique opportunity to influence the trajectory of autonomous flight tech.

- Fast-Paced Growth: Flat hierarchies and a decision-heavy environment —no red tape, just results.

- The Best Tools: Access to cutting-edge drone hardware and dedicated test facilities.

- Career Path: Development pathway toward Senior Flight Test Engineer or Test Director roles.

- Competitive Package: Salary that reflect your value to the mission.

postings.title: Werkstattmeister / Workshop Lead (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company, revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective.

Your mission

As our Werkstattmeister (Workshop Lead), you are the technical authority on the R&D shop floor. Your mission is to maintain a high-functioning prototyping environment that bridges the gap between digital design and physical testing.

You will lead a small team of 3–4 technicians and act as the "gatekeeper" of our workshop standards. You balance the speed of R&D with the necessity of order: you ensure tools are returned, machines are respected, and safety is never compromised. You aren't just a supervisor; you are an enabler who provides the guidance and structure engineers need to build and test their designs effectively before they move into series production.

Responsibilities

Workshop Management & Authority

- Ownership of the Floor: You define and enforce the standards for cleanliness, tool placement, and machine usage. You ensure the workshop remains organized enough to remain productive.

- Asset Maintenance: You own the maintenance cycles for our CNC portal, manual lathe, and large 3D printing farm (FDM, Resin, and SLS/PA11).

- Technical Guidance: You provide hands-on support and "over-the-shoulder" guidance to engineers. You ensure they use the equipment correctly and help them troubleshoot physical build issues.

- Inventory & Sourcing: You manage the stock of R&D materials and hardware. You will be a key stakeholder in selecting and commissioning our future high-end metal CNC machinery.

Prototyping & Assembly

- Execution: Lead the team in building complex prototypes, from UAV airframes to radio link towers and specialized test stands, supporting the Engineers that designed builds.

- Additive Farm Oversight: Ensure the printing farm is running efficiently, prioritizing jobs based on R&D needs and ensuring the quality of high-strength PA11 SLS parts.

- Process Transition: Help refine prototyping workflows so that designs can be successfully handed over to the production workshop.

Qualifications

Experience & Education

- Certified Master Craftsman (Meister) or Senior Technician in a mechanical field (e.g., Feinwerkmechanik, Industriemechanik, Modellbau, or Aviation/Fluggerätmechanik).

- Experience in a prototyping or R&D environment where you have managed both machines and people.

Technical Background

- Machining: Strong hands-on experience with manual lathes and CNC machines (milling/portal).

- Additive Manufacturing: Solid understanding of FDM and Resin processes. Practical experience with SLS (PA11) for functional parts is a strong advantage.

- Familiar with CAD/CAM: Ability to work with CATIA / 3DEXPERIENCE to review designs to prepare manufacturing steps is a plus.

- Standards: A background in aviation or defense-related manufacturing standards is a big plus.

Mindset & Working Style

- The "Anchor" of the Shop: You have the confidence to enforce shop floor rules and ensure discipline regarding tools and safety, but you do it to help the team, not to hinder them.

- Practical Leadership: You understand that R&D requires flexibility. You aim for a "clean-as-you-go" culture that supports speed rather than a rigid "sterile lab" mentality.

- Quality & Pride: You take personal pride in the state of the workshop and the quality of the prototypes that leave it.

postings.title: Werkstattmitarbeiter - Prototyping & Additive Manufacturing Technician (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company, revolutionizing the way autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. We design, develop and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective.

Your mission

As a Prototyping & Additive Manufacturing Technician, you are the "maker" who brings our digital designs into the physical world. Reporting to our Workshop/Prototyping Lead, you will be the primary operator of our R&D workshop equipment.

Your mission is to be the go-to person for rapid part production. Whether it’s managing a high-volume FDM print job, post-processing a high-strength SLS part, or machining a custom aluminum fixture on the CNC portal, you ensure that our engineers have the parts they need to test and iterate. You are self-sufficient, hands-on, and thrive in an environment where every day brings a different technical challenge.

Responsibilities

Additive Manufacturing & Print Farm Operations

- Print Farm Management: Take ownership of our FDM and Resin printer fleet. You handle everything from slicing and starting jobs to routine maintenance.

- SLS Production: Operate our large-scale SLS printer, managing the PA11 powder cycle and post-processing parts for high-strength applications.

- Quality Control: Ensure that printed parts meet the required tolerances and functional needs of the R&D team.

Machining & Prototyping

- CNC & Manual Machining: Operate our CNC portal machine, laser cutter, and manual lathe to produce one-off parts, fixtures, and components for UAVs and test stands.

- Rapid Prototyping: Support the assembly of complex sub-systems, such as radio link towers or launcher interfaces.

- Shop Support: Assist the Master in keeping the workshop functional. This includes organizing small parts, maintaining tools, and ensuring raw materials are ready for the next job.

Service & Efficiency

- Task Execution: Efficiently manage a queue of "small jobs" (e.g., "machine this bracket," "print this housing") and provide realistic timelines to the engineering team.

- Troubleshooting: Identify and solve issues with print failures or machining setups independently.

Qualifications

Experience & Background

- Technical Training: Completed vocational training as a Modellbauer, Industriemechaniker, Feinwerkmechaniker, or a similar technical field.

- Hands-on Experience: Proven track record in a workshop environment, ideally with a mix of additive manufacturing and traditional machining.

Technical Skills

- Additive Expert: Deep interest and experience in 3D printing (FDM is a must; Resin and SLS are huge pluses).

- Machinist Skills: Proficient in operating CNC machines and manual workshop tools. Experience with laser cutters is a benefit.

- CAD/CAM Literacy is a plus: Ability to open designs in CATIA / 3DEXPERIENCE and use slicing/CAM software to prepare jobs

- Manual Dexterity: You are "handy" and enjoy the fine details of assembling prototypes and finishing parts.

Mindset & Working Style

- Self-Sufficient: You see a job through from the initial request to the finished part with minimal supervision.

- Adaptable: You enjoy the variety of R&D—one day you are post-processing PA11 parts, the next you are turning a shaft on the lathe.

- Reliable: You understand that the engineering team depends on your speed and accuracy to hit their project milestones.

postings.title: Working Student – Flight Software Engineering (PX4 / Autopilot) (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a European defence technology company building the next generation of unmanned systems. We
design, develop and manufacture software-defined, mass-scalable and cost-effective platforms that give
NATO operators a decisive edge in highly contested environments. We are focused on delivering
deployable, high-performance capability — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, our work
strengthens the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners.

Your mission is to work hands-on with the software that flies our aircraft. You support the flight software
team on the PX4 / autopilot stack — writing and testing Python tooling, wrangling flight logs, and helping

postings.title: Working Student – Hardware Engineering (UAS Propulsion & Power) (all genders)
postings.description:
About Us

STARK is a European defence technology company building the next generation of unmanned systems. We
design, develop and manufacture software-defined, mass-scalable and cost-effective platforms that give
NATO operators a decisive edge in highly contested environments. We are focused on delivering
deployable, high-performance capability — not future promises. In a time of rising threats, our work
strengthens the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners.

About the team

You will join our hardware engineering team, working closely with engineers across propulsion, power systems, testing, and aircraft development to turn measured data into better-performing unmanned systems.

Your mission

Your mission is to work hands-on with the parts of the aircraft that turn stored energy into flight: the
motors, the batteries, and the propulsion and power components that decide how far, how fast, and how
long our platforms fly. You support the hardware team from bench characterisation through data analysis
in MATLAB and Python.

You aren't just swapping components on a bench; you are helping generate the measured evidence that
decides what actually flies — and learning how unmanned hardware is designed, tested, and pushed to its
limits.

Responsibilities

- Support characterisation and bench testing of motors, propellers, batteries, and power components for our UAS platforms.
- Help set up test rigs and instrumentation, and capture clean, repeatable measurement data.
- Assist with component selection and trade-offs by turning test data into clear comparisons.
- Reduce and analyse test data in MATLAB and Python — efficiency, thrust, endurance, thermal and discharge behaviour.
- Visualise results so the engineering team can make decisions from them quickly.
- Keep test setups, measurements, and findings documented and traceable.

Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace, or a comparable engineering field.
- Working knowledge of MATLAB and Python for data analysis.
- Interest in and some exposure to UAS, electric propulsion (motors / ESCs), or battery / power systems.
- Must be a citizen of a NATO member state (due to export control and security regulations).
- Practical, hands-on mindset — comfortable at the bench and with a multimeter as much as in a script.
- Good written and verbal communication skills in English; German is a plus.
- Hands-on: You like building, measuring, and finding out what really happens.
- Rigorous: You trust clean measurements over assumptions.
- Curious: You want to understand why a component behaves the way it does.

Nice to have

- Experience with test benches, DAQ, or measurement instrumentation.
- Familiarity with battery testing, thermal behaviour, or motor/propeller characterisation.
- Personal projects with drones, RC aircraft, batteries, or robotics.
